summary: On 12 June 2025 a third-party cloud provider that backs part of Workers KV's storage had its own outage. Workers KV failed for cold reads and writes, and Access, WARP, Gateway, Stream, Workers AI and many more services went down for about two and a half hours.

overview.background: Workers KV is a key-value service that many Cloudflare products use for configuration, authentication and asset delivery. It relies on a central data store as the source of truth, part of it backed by a third-party cloud provider.
systems: Workers KV and its central data store
Stream, Images, Realtime, Workers AI, Pages, Queues, D1 and more
overview.impact: About 90 percent of Workers KV requests failed when the value was not cached. Identity logins, WARP registrations, Stream playback, Workers AI inference and Pages builds were among the failures. Data stored was not lost.
overview.severity: A global incident of about 2 hours 28 to 36 minutes. Cloudflare says it was not an attack.
overview.gaps: The post states 2 hours 28 minutes but 17:52 to 20:28 is 2 hours 36 minutes. The last 5 KB of the page were not read.

timeline.e: The WARP team sees new device registrations failing and declares an incident.
The Access team is alerted to a rapid rise in error rates.
Service incidents are combined. The shared cause is Workers KV unavailability. Priority P1.
Zero Trust Gateway removes Workers KV dependencies by degrading rules that need identity or device posture.
Access and Device Posture force-drop identity and posture requests to shed load.
Services begin recovering. Caches repopulate and rate limits are hit.
Access and Device Posture resume calling Workers KV.
Impact ends and SLOs return to pre-incident levels.

rootCause.trigger: A failure in the third-party-backed storage underlying Workers KV.
rootCause.underlying: Workers KV's central store was a single source of truth, so its failure meant a complete outage of cold reads and writes. Cloudflare had gaps in resilience planning and was already moving KV to more resilient infrastructure.
contributing: Many products depended on KV for configuration and authentication
Some kill switches enabled during the incident allowed Turnstile tokens to be redeemed more than once
Caches repopulating caused rate limits during recovery
propagation: KV cold reads and writes fail.

evidence.label: The failure
evidence.body: A failure of that store caused a complete outage for cold reads and writes

evidence.label: Responsibility
evidence.body: we are ultimately responsible for our chosen dependencies and how we choose to architect around them.

evidence.label: A simulated degrade rule
evidence.body:
rule: gateway-identity-policy
on_kv_unavailable: skip-identity-conditions
log: degraded=true
evidence.note: Shows graceful degradation of a rule that needs identity. Invented.

diagnose.step: Find the shared failing dependency across products.
diagnose.why: KV unavailability was common to many incidents.
The third party had its own outage.

diagnose.step: Check which paths are cold versus cached.

correct.step: Combine incidents under one cause and raise priority.
Degrade or shed load for dependents.
Cut over critical namespaces to your own storage.
correct.why: Cloudflare began this during the incident.

prevent.step: Reduce the blast radius per product.

fix.safety: Kill switches can have security side effects. Review them before you rely on them in an incident.

troubleshoot.scenario: Many products fail at once. The shared dependency is a key-value service backed by a third-party store that is down.
troubleshoot.question: What do you do?
troubleshoot.answer: Combine incidents, degrade dependent products where safe, shed load from the store, shift critical data to your own storage, and re-enable gradually.

options: A third-party provider outage affecting KV storage

remediation.answer: Map each product to the stores it needs and the fallback.
Turn namespaces on in groups while watching load.
Document the security impact of each.

design.prompt: Design a key-value platform whose failure does not break logins.
design.answer: Use multiple storage backends, caches that survive outages, graceful degradation, per-product isolation and tested fallbacks.

checks.q: What share of uncached KV requests failed?
What did the dashboard login rely on?
What was Cloudflare moving KV toward?
